c2-job-0016: Job begins a search for wisdom. Peek at Job 28:1.
c2-job-0017: God understands the way of wisdom. Look at Job 28:8 and 23.
c3-job-0018: God knows wisdom's path and made the world His way. See Job 28:26 and 23.
c3-pro-0020: Wisdom takes her stand on a high hill. See Proverbs 8:15 and 2.
c3-ecc-0005: The Preacher looked for just the right words. Read Ecclesiastes 12:12 and 10.
c3-job-0019: Wisdom stands high. Job has more to say. See Job 28:7 and Proverbs 8:2.
c3-pro-0021: Iron comes from the earth. Wisdom blesses a listener. See Proverbs 8:34 and Job 28:2.
c3-ecc-0006: God knows that way. The Preacher honors wise words. See Ecclesiastes 12:11 and Job 28:23.
c3-job-0020: Every work will be judged. Job weighs wisdom's worth. See Job 28:18 and Ecclesiastes 12:14.
c3-pro-0022: The Preacher still taught people knowledge. Wisdom also speaks. See Proverbs 8:22 and Ecclesiastes 12:9.
c2-pro-0023: The sayings help a person understand a proverb. Peek at Proverbs 1:6.
c2-pro-0024: Proverbs talks about three that walk in a special way. See Proverbs 30:1 and 29.
c3-pro-0025: Do not take from the poor because they are poor. Check Proverbs 22:20 and 22.
c3-pro-0026: God pleads for the poor. Be careful of angry men. See Proverbs 22:25 and 23.
c3-pro-0027: Judge fairly, and help the poor and needy. Look at Proverbs 31:8 and 9.
c3-pro-0028: He names four of them, and three that walk well. See Proverbs 30:24 and 29.
c3-pro-0029: The writer says he feels less wise than other people. Check Proverbs 30:28 and 2.
c3-pro-0030: The book opens by talking about wisdom and instruction. Turn to Proverbs 22:21 and 1:2.
c3-pro-0031: Again we hear, do not take from the poor. Look at Proverbs 24:13 and 22:22.
c3-pro-0032: These are the proverbs of Solomon, son of David. Read Proverbs 30:32 and 1:1.
c2-hos-0009: The word of the LORD came to Hosea. Peek at Hosea 1:1.
c2-jol-0005: Joel received the word of the LORD. Peek at Joel 1:1.
c3-jon-0010: Jonah's opening tells how the word came. Read Jonah 1:1.
c3-nah-0004: Nahum wrote down a vision from God. Look at Nahum 1:1.
c3-zep-0006: The opening verse of Zephaniah is worth a close look. Check Zephaniah 1:1.
c3-oba-0004: Obadiah opens with a vision and a report from the LORD. See Obadiah 1:1.
c3-mic-0010: Micah calls the peoples to hear. I finally did. Turn to Micah 1:2.
c3-hab-0005: Habakkuk is sad when the wicked surround the righteous. Look at Habakkuk 1:4.
c3-jol-0006: Joel calls the elders and others to hear. Read Joel 1:2.
c3-jol-0010: Joel tells how the report should be passed down. Check Joel 1:3.
c2-zep-0011: Zephaniah talks about a very heavy day. Peek at Zephaniah 1:15.
c2-jol-0007: The One who carries out His word is strong. See Joel 2:5 and 11.
c3-amo-0010: Amos asks what good that day will be for some. Check Amos 5:19 and 18.
c3-zep-0007: Amos talks about a day with no brightness. Turn to Zephaniah 1:16 and Amos 5:20.
c3-jol-0008: That One is strong, and He carries out His word. See Joel 2:7 and 11.
c3-amo-0011: A strong One carries out His word. Amos speaks. See Amos 5:26 and Joel 2:11.
c3-jol-0009: Amos names a dark day. Joel speaks also. See Joel 2:21 and Amos 5:20.
c3-zep-0010: The great day of the LORD is near, says Zephaniah. Check Zephaniah 1:17 and 14.
c3-mal-0005: Joel says the people will eat and be satisfied. See Malachi 4:3 and Joel 2:26.
c3-amo-0012: His strong word will be carried out. See Amos 5:27 and Joel 2:11.
c2-isa-0028: Isaiah talks about the One who comes in righteousness. Peek at Isaiah 11:5.
c2-isa-0029: The remnant of Jacob will return. See Isaiah 10:20 and 21.
c3-mic-0011: Your hand shall be lifted against those who fight you. Check Micah 5:11 and 9.
c3-zep-0008: The LORD says He will save the lame. Turn to Zephaniah 3:18 and 19.
c3-zec-0009: These are the things you shall do, says the LORD. See Zechariah 8:10 and 16.
c3-isa-0030: Isaiah speaks of a highway for the remnant. Read Isaiah 11:11 and 16.
c3-mic-0012: The LORD says He will gather Jacob together. See Micah 2:13 and 12.
c3-zep-0009: A meek and humble people will be left among them. See Zephaniah 3:20 and 12.
c3-zec-0010: The LORD talks about the city's streets. Turn to Zechariah 8:5 and 16.
c3-isa-0031: A remnant of them will return. Look at Isaiah 11:15 and 10:22.
c2-1ki-0019: The people of Israel were divided into two parts. Peek at First Kings 16:21.
c2-1ki-0020: Elah was Baasha's son. Omri bought some land. See First Kings 16:24 and 8.
c3-1ki-0021: Zimri rose against Elah. Then Omri became king. Check First Kings 16:23 and 10.
c3-2ki-0021: Jehoash was Jehoahaz's son. Shallum also ruled awhile. See Second Kings 15:13 and 13:10.
c3-2ki-0022: A man went up from Tirzah in those days. See Second Kings 15:23 and 14.
c3-2ki-0023: The LORD gave Israel into Hazael's hand. See Second Kings 15:27 and 13:3.
c3-2ki-0024: The LORD struck a king, and his life changed. See Second Kings 15:5 and 13:10.
c3-2ch-0007: Uzziah sought God in Zechariah's days and built towers. See Second Chronicles 26:9 and 5.
c3-2ch-0008: Jotham built cities in Judah's hills. Uzziah built too. See Second Chronicles 26:15 and 27:4.
c3-2ch-0009: Jotham's years as king are written down. Look at Second Chronicles 27:6 and 8.
c2-ezr-0008: Cyrus brought the temple articles out. Peek at Ezra 1:8.
c2-neh-0009: It was the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes. See Nehemiah 1:1 and 2:1.
c3-neh-0010: The king asked how long the journey would be. See Nehemiah 2:8 and 6.
c3-est-0008: Mordecai was well received by many of his people. Turn to Esther 1:1 and 10:3.
c3-est-0009: Haman had a plan, and a lot was cast. Look at Esther 3:7 and 10:3.
c3-est-0010: Mordecai wrote these things and sent letters to the Jews. Read Esther 9:31 and 20.
c3-hag-0005: They were helped with silver and gold. See Haggai 1:1 and Ezra 1:6.
c3-zec-0011: Ezra begins a count with thirty gold platters. See Zechariah 1:1 and Ezra 1:9.
c3-zec-0012: Malachi brought a word to Israel. Zechariah speaks too. See Zechariah 1:5 and Malachi 1:1.
c3-ezr-0009: Men back home should help with silver and gold. See Ezra 1:11 and 4.
